key_insight: Mobile ions have only a small effect on steady-state performance in efficient perovskite solar cells, even though their influence can vary with device properties.
engineering_relevance: For device design, this suggests steady-state efficiency is driven more by materials parameters such as recombination and band offsets than by ion mobility in already optimized cells.
method: Drift-diffusion simulations of paired perovskite solar cells
601 matched device pairs: one with mobile ions, one without
Factorial analysis across ion density, recombination rate, band offsets, and contact-layer/device architecture
evidence_signal: The study evaluates 1202 simulated cells total across a broad range of physically relevant parameters to isolate the effect of mobile ions.
watch_item: Results are based on steady-state modelling, so transient effects and real-device degradation mechanisms may not be captured.
paper_title: An Investigation into the Effect of Mobile Ions on the Steady State Performance of Perovskite Solar Cells
